answer: Cheap aliases collapse when admission needs a living plant and a one-use punch. The applicant stakes 28 coins, grafts a numbered tag onto a posted-bank willow, then takes a leaf-print rubbing to a night-shift forge where a seed-chosen die is struck into a tin disc in 16 minutes. The disc sits in a clerk-watched vault cell for 11 days. Two clerks who have never co-signed this applicant hash the graft scar, punch depth, and cell number. The bond returns only if both hashes match and the die serial is unused. Reusing the tree or cell burns both stakes, so each alias needs a fresh tree and cell.
